prompt: Some people believe that violence on television and in computer games has a damaging effect on children. Others deny that these factors have any significant influence on how children behave. Discuss both sides and give your opinion.
essay:
The impact of media violence on young minds is a subject of intense debate. While some argue that aggressive content in television programs and video games severely harms children, others believe its influence is negligible. This essay will examine both perspectives before explaining why I believe media violence poses a genuine risk to adolescent behaviour

On the one hand, opponents of the media-damage theory argue that screen entertainment is merely a form of harmless escapism. They primarily believe that children can easily distinguish between fictional violence and real-world interactions. Furthermore, modern psychologists often highlight the "catharsis theory," which suggests that virtual combat allows youth to release pent-up frustration in a safe, simulated environment. From this perspective, playing a violent game or watching an action movie serves as a healthy emotional outlet rather than a catalyst for real-world hostility.

On the other hand, there is compelling evidence that consistent exposure to violent media desensitises children.  First, young people who repeatedly witness aggressive acts on screen  begin to view violence as a normal mechanism for conflict resolution. For instance, numerous psychological studies demonstrate that children who play first-person shooter games exhibit higher levels of immediate physical aggression and reduced empathy toward peers. Moreover, children naturally learn through imitation. Witnessing rewarded aggression in virtual worlds can easily translate into bullying and behavioural issues in the playground.

In conclusion, although some view media violence as benign entertainment that promotes emotional release, I believe it acts as a dangerous blueprint for aggressive behaviour. In my opinion, the negative influence of media violence cannot be dismissed. While a stable child might not become a criminal overnight, continuous exposure gradually erodes their moral filters and normalises aggression
